name: Expenses document date for later period v/s posting date in previous period / qtr
description: Flag line items where Document Date falls in a later accounting month-year than Posting Date, including across years, indicating potential timing irregularities.

data.plan: 1. WORKFLOW PURPOSE This workflow identifies expense line items where the document’s originating date occurs in a later accounting month than the posting date recorded in SAP. Such timing differences can indicate back‑dating, delayed posting, or mis‑allocation of expenses across periods, which may affect period‑end reporting, budgeting, and compliance with internal control policies. By flagging every instance where the Document Date is at least one month later than the Posting Date, finance and audit teams obtain a focused list of transactions that require review to confirm legitimate business reasons (e.g., receipt of a late invoice) or to uncover potential policy violations. 2. INPUT REQUIREMENTS The workflow requires the following input file: • FBL3N.csv: Export of the SAP General Ledger line‑item table (FBL3N). It contains transactional details for each expense line, including dates, amounts, account numbers, cost and profit centers, and reference information needed for root‑cause analysis. 3. BUSINESS LOGIC STEPS 1. Load the FBL3N.csv file and verify that all required columns are present. 2. Convert the three date fields – Document Date, Posting Date, and Entry Date – into proper date formats for calculation. 3. Derive a month‑year string for both Document Date and Posting Date (e.g., “2024‑06”). 4. Calculate the whole‑month difference between Document Date and Posting Date:     Month Difference = (Document Year – Posting Year) × 12 + (Document Month – Posting Month). 5. Create two flags that indicate whether the month shift crosses a fiscal quarter or a calendar year. 6. Apply the exception filter: keep only rows where the Month Difference is ≥ 1 (i.e., the document is dated in a later month). 7. Assemble the final result set, preserving all original identifiers and adding the calculated month‑year, month‑difference, and crossing‑quarter/year flags. 8. Export the flagged records to a CSV file for review by finance and audit stakeholders. 4. EXCEPTION CRITERIA An exception is flagged when: • Condition 1: The calculated month difference (Document Date minus Posting Date) is **greater than or equal to 1**, meaning the document’s date falls in a later month than the posting period. • Condition 2: No materiality or amount threshold is applied – every line item meeting Condition 1 is flagged, regardless of the amount’s size, sign, or whether the amount is zero. These conditions matter because any post‑period document date may indicate timing manipulation, delayed receipt of supporting documentation, or errors in period‑closing processes, all of which can distort financial results and undermine audit trails. 5. OUTPUT DESCRIPTION The results file lists each flagged line item with the following columns and business meanings: • Company Code: Legal entity to which the transaction belongs; used for routing and consolidation. • Document Number: Unique identifier of the accounting document; enables retrieval of the full source record. • Posting Key: Indicates debit or credit nature of the line item. • G/L Account: General Ledger account affected; shows the financial statement line impacted. • G/L Acct Long Text: Descriptive text of the G/L account for easier interpretation. • G/L Acct Long Text.1: Alternate or extended account description where available. • Cost Center: Operational cost owner; helps pinpoint responsibility for the expense. • Profit Center: Profitability segment; useful for assessing impact on profit reporting. • Document Date: Original date on the source document (invoice, receipt, etc.). • Posting Date: Accounting period date used for posting the transaction in SAP. • Amount in local currency: Transaction amount in the company’s functional currency, preserving sign and magnitude. • Document currency: Currency in which the original document was issued. • Document Type: Classification of the transaction (e.g., invoice, credit memo, journal). • Text: Line‑item free‑text field that may contain explanatory notes. • Document Header Text: Header‑level narrative providing context for the whole document. • Reference: External reference such as invoice number or purchase order. • Assignment: Additional reference field for grouping related items. • Offsett.account type: Type of the offsetting account (vendor, customer, etc.). • Offsetting acct no.: Account number of the counterpart in the transaction. • Supplier: Name or identifier of the supplier, when applicable. • Purchasing Document: Link to the procurement document (e.g., PO) for cross‑validation. • Entry Date: Date the transaction was entered into the system, providing operational timing context. • User Name: SAP user who posted the line item; useful for process accountability. • Document Month-Year_Calculated: Derived month‑year of the Document Date (e.g., “2024‑06”). • Posting Month-Year_Calculated: Derived month‑year of the Posting Date. • Month Difference_Calculated: Numeric count of whole months the Document Date is later than the Posting Date. • Cross Quarter Flag_Calculated: “Y” if the month shift crosses a fiscal quarter boundary; otherwise “N”. • Cross Year Flag_Calculated: “Y” if the month shift crosses a calendar‑year boundary; otherwise “N”. 6. BUSINESS IMPACT Why This Check Is Important: Identifying expense entries that are dated in a period later than the posting period protects the integrity of period‑end closing, ensures that expenses are recognized in the correct fiscal period, and supports compliance with accounting standards (e.g., accrual principle). It also provides early warning of potential manipulation or process breakdowns that could lead to misstated financial statements or audit findings. Risks Identified: • Mis‑stated expense recognition that can affect profitability and budgeting. • Potential back‑dating of invoices to manipulate performance metrics or meet internal targets. • Weaknesses in the invoice‑receipt‑posting workflow that may cause delayed postings or missed cut‑offs. Recommended Actions: • Investigate each flagged transaction to determine whether a legitimate business reason (e.g., late receipt of an invoice) exists. • Document the justification and, if appropriate, adjust posting dates or create proper accrual entries. • Review and strengthen the controls around invoice receipt, verification, and timely posting to reduce recurrence. • Provide training to posting users on the importance of aligning document and posting dates with fiscal period rules. • Periodically run this workflow as part of the month‑end control checklist and report findings to the internal audit function.

# ===========================================================================
# PART 1: IMPORT LIBRARIES & FILE PATH VARIABLES
# ===========================================================================

import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
from datetime import datetime, timedelta
import os
import ira

fbl3n_path = "/Users/ajay/Documents/workflow_builder_v4/data/uploads/6a26da2d-84df-4970-af43-9a0ee70035e9/FBL3N.csv"
output_file_path = "/Users/ajay/Documents/workflow_builder_v4/data/outputs/Expenses_document_date_for_later_period_v/s_posting_date_in_previous_period_/_qtr/output_1b9f31d3-1243-40a3-95e6-4e3b8ed9c7cf.csv"


# ===========================================================================
# PART 2: LOAD DATAFRAMES & IRA PREPROCESSING
# ===========================================================================

# Column categories for FBL3N
DATE_COLS_FBL3N = ['Document Date', 'Posting Date', 'Entry Date']
SAME_COLS_FBL3N = []          # No same‑case string columns needed for this workflow
UPPER_COLS_FBL3N = []         # No upper‑case string columns needed
LOWER_COLS_FBL3N = []         # No lower‑case string columns needed
TITLE_COLS_FBL3N = []         # No title‑case string columns needed
NUMERIC_COLS_FBL3N = ['Amount in local currency']

# Load FBL3N data
df_fbl3n = pd.read_csv(fbl3n_path, low_memory=False)
print(f"✓ Loaded {len(df_fbl3n):,} rows from FBL3N")

# Verify required source columns
required_columns_fbl3n = [
    "Company Code", "Document Number", "Posting Key", "G/L Account",
    "G/L Acct Long Text", "G/L Acct Long Text.1", "Cost Center", "Profit Center",
    "Document Date", "Posting Date", "Amount in local currency", "Document currency",
    "Document Type", "Text", "Document Header Text", "Reference", "Assignment",
    "Offsett.account type", "Offsetting acct no.", "Supplier", "Purchasing Document",
    "Entry Date", "User Name"
]
missing_columns = [col for col in required_columns_fbl3n if col not in df_fbl3n.columns]
if missing_columns:
    raise ValueError(f"Missing columns in FBL3N: {missing_columns}")

# IRA preprocessing for FBL3N
for col in DATE_COLS_FBL3N:
    if col in df_fbl3n.columns:
        df_fbl3n[col] = ira.convert_date_column(df_fbl3n[col])

if SAME_COLS_FBL3N:
    df_fbl3n = ira.clean_strings_batch(df_fbl3n, SAME_COLS_FBL3N, rules={
        "remove_excel_artifacts": True,
        "normalize_whitespace": True,
        "case_mode": "same"
    })

if UPPER_COLS_FBL3N:
    df_fbl3n = ira.clean_strings_batch(df_fbl3n, UPPER_COLS_FBL3N, rules={
        "remove_excel_artifacts": True,
        "normalize_whitespace": True,
        "case_mode": "upper"
    })

if LOWER_COLS_FBL3N:
    df_fbl3n = ira.clean_strings_batch(df_fbl3n, LOWER_COLS_FBL3N, rules={
        "remove_excel_artifacts": True,
        "normalize_whitespace": True,
        "case_mode": "lower"
    })

if TITLE_COLS_FBL3N:
    df_fbl3n = ira.clean_strings_batch(df_fbl3n, TITLE_COLS_FBL3N, rules={
        "remove_excel_artifacts": True,
        "normalize_whitespace": True,
        "case_mode": "title"
    })

if NUMERIC_COLS_FBL3N:
    df_fbl3n = ira.clean_numeric_batch(df_fbl3n, NUMERIC_COLS_FBL3N)

print(f"✓ IRA preprocessing complete for FBL3N")


# ===========================================================================
# PART 3: BUSINESS LOGIC
# ===========================================================================

# -------------------------------------------------
# Step 1: Derive month‑year strings for Document and Posting dates
# -------------------------------------------------
df_fbl3n['Document Month-Year_Calculated'] = df_fbl3n['Document Date'].dt.to_period('M').astype(str)
df_fbl3n['Posting Month-Year_Calculated']   = df_fbl3n['Posting Date'].dt.to_period('M').astype(str)

# -------------------------------------------------
# Step 2: Calculate whole‑month difference (Document – Posting)
# -------------------------------------------------
df_fbl3n['Month Difference_Calculated'] = (
    (df_fbl3n['Document Date'].dt.year - df_fbl3n['Posting Date'].dt.year) * 12 +
    (df_fbl3n['Document Date'].dt.month - df_fbl3n['Posting Date'].dt.month)
)

# -------------------------------------------------
# Step 3: Flags for crossing quarter / year boundaries
# -------------------------------------------------
df_fbl3n['Cross Quarter Flag_Calculated'] = np.where(
    df_fbl3n['Document Date'].dt.quarter != df_fbl3n['Posting Date'].dt.quarter,
    'Y', 'N'
)

df_fbl3n['Cross Year Flag_Calculated'] = np.where(
    df_fbl3n['Document Date'].dt.year != df_fbl3n['Posting Date'].dt.year,
    'Y', 'N'
)

print("✓ Calculated month‑year fields, month difference, and crossing flags")

# -------------------------------------------------
# Step 4: Filter for exceptions (Document month later than Posting month by ≥ 1)
# -------------------------------------------------
exception_df = df_fbl3n[df_fbl3n['Month Difference_Calculated'] >= 1].copy()
print(f"✓ Applied exception filter: {len(exception_df):,} flagged rows")

# -------------------------------------------------
# Step 5: Select and order final output columns
# -------------------------------------------------
output_columns = [
    "Company Code", "Document Number", "Posting Key", "G/L Account",
    "G/L Acct Long Text", "G/L Acct Long Text.1", "Cost Center", "Profit Center",
    "Document Date", "Posting Date", "Amount in local currency", "Document currency",
    "Document Type", "Text", "Document Header Text", "Reference", "Assignment",
    "Offsett.account type", "Offsetting acct no.", "Supplier", "Purchasing Document",
    "Entry Date", "User Name", "Document Month-Year_Calculated",
    "Posting Month-Year_Calculated", "Month Difference_Calculated",
    "Cross Quarter Flag_Calculated", "Cross Year Flag_Calculated"
]

# Ensure all required output columns exist (calculated ones have just been added)
missing_output = [col for col in output_columns if col not in exception_df.columns]
if missing_output:
    raise ValueError(f"Missing columns in final output: {missing_output}")

result_df = exception_df[output_columns].reset_index(drop=True)

# -------------------------------------------------
# Validation
# -------------------------------------------------
if result_df.empty:
    print("⚠ Warning: No exceptions detected – result dataframe is empty.")
else:
    print(f"✓ Final result prepared: {len(result_df):,} rows, {len(result_df.columns)} columns")

# -------------------------------------------------
# Save to CSV
# -------------------------------------------------
os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(output_file_path), exist_ok=True)
result_df.to_csv(output_file_path, index=False)
print(f"✓ SUCCESS: Saved results to {output_file_path}")

required_cols = [

]
missing = [c for c in required_cols if c not in df.columns]
if missing:

# ===========================================================================
# PART 3: ANALYSIS & REPORT GENERATION
# ===========================================================================

report_lines = []

# Header
report_lines.append("=" * 80)
report_lines.append("WORKFLOW ANALYSIS REPORT")
report_lines.append(
    "Workflow: Expenses document date for later period vs posting date in previous period / qtr"
)
report_lines.append(f"Generated on: {datetime.now().strftime('%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S')}")
report_lines.append("=" * 80)
report_lines.append("")

# --------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Exception Summary
# --------------------------------------------------------------------
total_exceptions = len(df)
if total_exceptions == 0:
    report_lines.append("No exceptions identified.")
    report_content = "\n".join(report_lines)
    os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(output_file_path), exist_ok=True)

        f.write(report_content)

    print(f"✓ Report written to {output_file_path}")
    raise SystemExit

report_lines.append("1. Exception Summary")
report_lines.append(f"Total exceptions: {total_exceptions:,}")
report_lines.append("")

# --------------------------------------------------------------------
# Helper to get top N value_counts as a formatted string
# --------------------------------------------------------------------
def format_top_counts(series, top_n=5, name=""):
    vc = series.value_counts(dropna=False).head(top_n)
    lines = [f"Top {len(vc)} {name}:"] if name else []
    for val, cnt in vc.items():
        display_val = "<missing>" if pd.isna(val) else str(val)
        lines.append(f"  {display_val}: {cnt:,}")
    return "\n".join(lines)

# --------------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Key Dimension‑Based Trends
# --------------------------------------------------------------------
report_lines.append("2. Key Dimension‑Based Trends")

# Company Code
report_lines.append(format_top_counts(df["Company Code"], top_n=5, name="Company Codes"))
report_lines.append("")

# G/L Account
report_lines.append(format_top_counts(df["G/L Account"], top_n=5, name="G/L Accounts"))

# Cross Year Flag_Calculated

                                      name="Cross Year Flag (Y/N)"))

# --------------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. Time‑Based Trends (Month/Quarter)
# --------------------------------------------------------------------
report_lines.append("3. Time‑Based Trends (Month/Quarter)")

# Count per month
month_counts = df["Posting Month-Year_Calculated"].value_counts().sort_index()
peak_month = month_counts.idxmax()
peak_month_cnt = month_counts.max()
report_lines.append(
    f"Peak month: {peak_month} with {peak_month_cnt:,} exceptions"
)

# Derive quarter
month_dt = pd.to_datetime(df["Posting Month-Year_Calculated"], format="%Y-%m", errors="coerce")
df["_Quarter"] = month_dt.dt.to_period("Q").astype(str)

quarter_counts = df["_Quarter"].value_counts().sort_index()
if not quarter_counts.empty:
    peak_quarter = quarter_counts.idxmax()
    peak_quarter_cnt = quarter_counts.max()
    report_lines.append(
        f"Peak quarter: {peak_quarter} with {peak_quarter_cnt:,} exceptions"
    )
else:
    report_lines.append("Quarter information could not be derived.")
report_lines.append("")

amount_series = df["Amount in local currency"]
total_amount = amount_series.sum()
avg_amount = amount_series.mean()
min_amount = amount_series.min()
max_amount = amount_series.max()

report_lines.append(f"Average amount: {avg_amount:,.2f}")
report_lines.append(f"Minimum amount: {min_amount:,.2f}")
report_lines.append(f"Maximum amount: {max_amount:,.2f}")

# Breakdown by top Company Code (the most frequent one)
top_company = df["Company Code"].value_counts().idxmax()
company_mask = df["Company Code"] == top_company
company_total = amount_series[company_mask].sum()
company_avg = amount_series[company_mask].mean()
report_lines.append(
    f"\nAmount for top Company Code ({top_company}): total {company_total:,.2f}, "
    f"average {company_avg:,.2f}"
)
report_lines.append("")

# --------------------------------------------------------------------
# 5. Statistical / Numeric Insight (optional)

    mean_amt = amount_series.mean()
    median_amt = amount_series.median()
    std_amt = amount_series.std()
    outlier_threshold = mean_amt + 3 * std_amt
    outliers = df[amount_series > outlier_threshold]

    report_lines.append(f"Mean amount: {mean_amt:,.2f}")
    report_lines.append(f"Median amount: {median_amt:,.2f}")
    report_lines.append(f"Standard deviation: {std_amt:,.2f}")
    report_lines.append(f"Outlier threshold (mean + 3σ): {outlier_threshold:,.2f}")
    report_lines.append(f"Number of outliers: {len(outliers):,}")

    # Correlation
    if "Month Difference_Calculated" in df.columns:
        corr = amount_series.corr(df["Month Difference_Calculated"])
        report_lines.append(
            f"Pearson correlation between Amount and Month Difference: {corr:.4f}"
        )
        # Simple linear regression (Amount = a * MonthDiff + b)
        try:
            slope, intercept = np.polyfit(
                df["Month Difference_Calculated"], amount_series, 1
            )
            # Compute R^2
            predicted = slope * df["Month Difference_Calculated"] + intercept
            ss_res = np.sum((amount_series - predicted) ** 2)
            ss_tot = np.sum((amount_series - mean_amt) ** 2)
            r_squared = 1 - ss_res / ss_tot if ss_tot != 0 else np.nan
            report_lines.append(
                f"Regression: Amount = {slope:.4f} * MonthDiff + {intercept:.2f} "
                f"(R² = {r_squared:.4f})"
            )
        except Exception as e:

    report_lines.append("")
else:

# --------------------------------------------------------------------

report_lines.append(f"- Highest exception count company: {top_company}")

report_lines.append(f"- Peak posting period: {peak_month}")
if total_exceptions >= 30 and len(outliers) > 0:
    report_lines.append(
        f"- Detected {len(outliers):,} monetary outlier(s) exceeding 3σ."
    )
report_lines.append(
    "Recommended next steps: review documents for the top cost centres, "
    "investigate large‑value outliers and any cross‑year postings."
)
report_lines.append("")

# --------------------------------------------------------------------
# Finalise report
# --------------------------------------------------------------------
report_content = "\n".join(report_lines)

# Ensure output directory exists
os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(output_file_path), exist_ok=True)

# Write report to text file
with open(output_file_path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
    f.write(report_content)

print(f"✓ SUCCESS: Analysis report saved to {output_file_path}")
print("TERMINATE")
